newsitem.title: CHINA: China Q1 retail price inflation forecast at 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Q1 retail price inflation forecast at 3 pct.

text.p: China's retail price inflation for the first quarter is forecast to have fallen to three percent year-on-year, Premier Li Peng said on Wednesday.

"The forecast for the retail price inflation rate in the first quarter is that it will fall further to around three percent," Li told the opening ceremony of the International Chamber of Commerce meeting being held in Shanghai.
China's year-on-year retail price inflation in 1996 was 6.1 percent, while the year-on-year growth in gross domestic product (GDP) was 9.7 percent, Li said.
He welcomed the hundreds of business executives from around the world attending the congress, saying the choice of Shanghai as a venue was an expression of confidence in China's strong growth.
"China's economic development is closely tied to the prosperity of Asia," Li said, adding that Asia would find its own path to economic prosperity.
"Asian countries never impose their own views on others and oppose the practice of interference in the internal affairs of other countries," he added.
